summary: Pender County entry on the NC tower list, separate from the Bannerman tower. No source found on its build, height or condition today.

evidence.supports: Rocky Point is its own entry in Pender County
Bannerman is a separate entry, farther north
A waymark listing is titled Rocky Point Fire Tower
evidence.quote: Rocky Point Fire Tower - Look-Out Towers on Waymarking.com

evidence.supports: Bannerman tower: 80-foot steel tower near Bannerman's Bridge, built 1927 with the Cooper River Timber Company and the State Division of Forest Resources
evidence.quote: 1927: An 80-foot steel tower near Bannerman's Bridge was built by Cooper River Timber Company in a cooperative effort with the State Division of Forest Resources.

evidence.supports: March 2018 surplus auction; the Bannerman tower is on state-owned property
evidence.quote: March 22, 2018: Auction opened for bids on surplus state property. The tower is located on state owned property.

corrections.why: The NC list keeps Bannerman (34.59166,-77.80027) and Rocky Point (34.45611,-77.88277) as separate entries, and the Bannerman page describes a different 80-foot tower.
24.4 m is 80 ft, the height the Bannerman page gives for the Bannerman tower. No source found gives a height for the Rocky Point entry.

notes_for_editor: Likely record error: other_names 'Bannerman' and height_m 24.4 (80 ft) appear to come from the separate Bannerman tower, which the TN Landforms list keeps apart and the Bannerman page describes. Corrections are proposed for human review, not applied. No source found gives Rocky Point's own build date, height, staffing, status or agency; the record's NC DFR agency is not supported for this entry. The Waymarking page text read was only its title. A Wilmington Star-News 2019 article on Pender County fire towers returned 403 and was not read. Access is unknown. Confidence low; the story is short because the sources are.
